trust_decision.summary: Whether Google OAuth access/refresh tokens are encrypted before they are persisted. At the pinned commit they are not: they are written in plain text to User.googleTokens by the sign-in event and the token-refresh writer, and to the Account row by the Auth.js Prisma adapter.

landing_point.why: The Auth.js signIn event writes the tokens into User.googleTokens as a plain JSON object, even though the schema comment says 'Encrypted GSC OAuth tokens' (prisma/schema.prisma:18). This is the first place a reader of 'cleartext storage of Google OAuth tokens' would look.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/auth/callback/google (Auth.js events.signIn via app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts), now calls storeSignInTokens (fix.diff:1219)

Any GSC call that triggers a refresh: getAccessToken from lib/google/gsc-client.ts:34, lib/google/gsc-client.ts:67, lib/google/gsc-client.ts:148, lib/google/url-inspection-client.ts:37 (GSC sync/properties API routes, MCP tools). The refresh write is sealed (fix.diff:1642-1649)
Same getAccessToken callers. The read is changed to decrypt and to accept legacy plain rows; an undecryptable row raises ReauthRequiredError (fix.diff:1620-1631)
GET /api/auth/callback/google: PrismaAdapter.linkAccount writes access_token/refresh_token in plain text to the Account row. The fix clears them after sign-in (fix.diff:1941-1944)
fix_sites.module_kind: third-party adapter (Auth.js Prisma adapter) data producer

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI: npx tsx scripts/encrypt-google-tokens.ts [--apply] (fix.diff:1996-2012), a new migration for legacy plain-text rows and Account copies
New lib/google/token-store.ts (seal/open/isSealed/storeSignInTokens), used by every site above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: prisma/schema.prisma:35-36: a second at-rest copy of the same tokens in the Account row, written by PrismaAdapter(db) (lib/auth.ts:18) during the OAuth callback, before and outside the app's events.signIn (lib/auth.ts:44). Also legacy plain User.googleTokens rows, which are read back by lib/google/google-auth.ts:77 and re-sealed only on refresh or by the migration (fix.diff:1642-1649, fix.diff:1532-1582)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Account table belongs to Auth.js's adapter schema and is 'library-managed'. Nothing in the app reads tokens from it, and the row must stay for returning-user recognition (lib/registration.ts:16-25), so a solver can argue that touching it is out of scope or risks breaking sign-in. Legacy rows can be argued to be a data migration, not a code fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several things must keep working. The Account row must survive (DISABLE_REGISTRATION recognises returning users by it). Non-secret fields (expiresAt, scope, tokenType) must stay readable for the expiry check and the scope display. Legacy plain-text rows must still be read, without forcing a re-auth. Already-sealed values must not be encrypted twice. An over-broad fix would delete the Account row, encrypt the whole JSON (breaking expiresAt checks), or reject legacy rows.

O6_input_shapes: new sign-in tokens object (accessToken + refreshToken + expiresAt/tokenType/scope)
refresh write spreading an existing stored object with a new accessToken/expiresAt
legacy plain-text stored object read as is
already-prefixed (enc:v1:) values left unchanged (no double seal)
non-object or array stored value treated as none
value sealed with another secret (undecryptable), mapped to ReauthRequiredError
Account-row copy (snake_case access_token/refresh_token columns) vs User.googleTokens (camelCase JSON)

O7_producer.where: lib/auth.ts:18 PrismaAdapter(db): the Auth.js adapter's linkAccount maps the OAuth account to the Account row (prisma/schema.prisma:35-40) inside the callback, before events.signIn

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Account.id_token (Google OIDC ID token) stays in plain text after sign-in: the published sign-in cleanup nulls only access_token and refresh_token, while the new disconnect path also nulls id_token
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: An ID token is an identity assertion, not an API credential, and it expires quickly. The published fix itself leaves it at sign-in (fix.diff:1941-1944 vs fix.diff:1155-1158).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same callback route as the landing point; written by a third-party adapter

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The refresh response handler also persists a rotated refresh_token when Google returns one, via a separate db.user.update
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Google can rotate refresh tokens; a maintainer adding rotation support would write a second googleTokens update next to the existing one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A standalone MCP-process token loader/writer that reads or refreshes User.googleTokens directly instead of going through getAccessToken
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The MCP server runs as a separate process (package.json:27; fix.diff:1347-1349), so a maintainer could plausibly add its own token handling there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The demo seeder writes placeholder or copied googleTokens for the demo user
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Seeders often populate auth fields so GSC pages render; it is a CLI path far from the auth code.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'reconnect Google' or import endpoint next to the API-key settings that accepts and stores Google tokens
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The settings area already stores encrypted third-party credentials, so a token import or reconnect route would sit naturally beside it.

O9_family: CWE-312 cleartext storage of sensitive information (OAuth credentials at rest; secret-at-rest/crypto-application family)
